second_review.operative_ask: The administration, with funding from Congress, should fund the design, development and deployment of new warheads including pit production in quantity, continue developing new warheads for each triad leg, maintain two pit production sites at Los Alamos and Savannah River, reverse the B83 retirement and the sea-launched cruise missile cancellation if possible, and target funds to accelerated warhead development, drawing first on DOE non-nuclear programs (pages 372, 398 to 400).
second_review.rule_applied: Implemented at the band floor. Test (a): the operative instruments of the ask are funding, continuation and maintenance, and these are in effect in substance: the two-site plan continues and, per a pre-enactment summary, is codified in the FY2026 NDAA; plutonium modernization, the W93 and W87-1 programs and the sea-launched cruise missile and its warhead are funded through P.L. 119-21 and FY2026 measures. Test (b): nothing is opposite to the ask; the B83 reversal is not shown and was qualified by the text as if possible. Test (c): funding requires Congress, and Congress has provided it. Quantity pit output is years away, but page 372 asks that such production be funded and pages 398 to 399 ask that two sites be maintained, not that a numeric milestone be met, so the missing output keeps the record at the floor rather than in in_progress.

status_summary: The two-site plutonium pit approach has continued: NNSA published a notice of intent for a programmatic environmental impact statement covering Los Alamos and Savannah River on 2025-05-09, and the draft became available on 2026-04-17, with comments open to 2026-07-16 and a final statement planned for early 2027. Section 3112 of Public Law 119-60 (FY2026 NDAA, enacted 2025-12-18) adds a statutory capacity provision under which Los Alamos is to be able to produce at least 30 war reserve pits a year and Savannah River at least 50, with no deadline stated, and Public Law 119-21 (2025-07-04) provided 2 billion dollars for the nuclear sea-launched cruise missile and 400 million dollars for its warhead, per CRS, which also notes statutory deployment dates of 2032 and 2034. Trade press reported on 2026-01-29 that Los Alamos exceeded its pit production objectives and is working toward 30 pits per year by 2028, and Arms Control Today reported in September 2026 that construction of the Savannah River facility remains at an early stage, with completion expected between late 2031 and mid-2035. The stage is implemented because the funding, continued warhead development and two-site posture the text asks for are in effect, while quantity production is years away and no action on the B83 retirement was found.

timeline.event: NNSA published a notice of intent to prepare a programmatic environmental impact statement for plutonium pit production, with single-site and multi-site alternatives at Los Alamos and Savannah River.
Public Law 119-21 enacted; per CRS it includes 2 billion dollars for the nuclear sea-launched cruise missile and 400 million dollars to accelerate its warhead.

The National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026 (S. 1071) is enacted as Public Law 119-60; Section 3112 amends 50 U.S.C. 2538a to require that Los Alamos have the capability to produce at least 30 war reserve pits a year and the Savannah River Plutonium Processing Facility at least 50, with no deadline stated.
EPA published the notice of availability of the draft pit production programmatic environmental impact statement, opening a 90-day comment period to 2026-07-16, with public hearings in May 2026.

title: Fund new warheads, keep two plutonium pit sites, revive sea-launched cruise missile
uncertainties: Pit counts are classified, so progress rests on official statements relayed by trade press. The text of Section 3112 of Public Law 119-60 was read only in a reproduction of the GPO slip-law pages (139 Stat. 1462-1463) hosted by the Los Alamos Study Group, a non-government site; the govinfo.gov copy ends before Division C and the Cornell LII copy of 50 U.S.C. 2538a had not been updated for the amendment, so the wording was not compared against a government-hosted copy. The DOE hearing presentation (energy.gov) says a court settlement requires a record of decision on a set schedule; that litigation was not traced. A search for any decision to keep the B83 found nothing conclusive. A Center for Arms Control summary (armscontrolcenter.org, 2025-12-12) of the conference text also describes 210 million dollars for the cruise missile and 50 million dollars for its warhead and continued W93 and W87-1 funding; it is an advocacy summary used as a lead only, and those amounts were not checked in the enacted text. The Los Alamos production report (Exchange Monitor, 2026-01-29) and the Savannah River construction report (Arms Control Today, September 2026) are reports of status, not government actions, and are kept as sources rather than timeline events. Arms Control Today (September 2026, day not given) reports officials saying Los Alamos output could be accelerated by 2028 and an internal review of pit plans requested in the FY2026 appropriations act. Much of the two-site posture and warhead work predates 2025-01-20 and continues; the record reports alignment, not new causation. Overlaps the DoD-chapter record c04-06 on pits and the cruise missile.
